    ZeRO-2 CPU offload: accumulate in the compact partition between requests (#9044)
    
    ## Summary
    
    Follow-up to #9018 (merged as `a4c989b7`). With CPU offload, the compact
    partition-sized accumulator (used for fp32 accumulation on a 16-bit
    model) now publishes to the host partition gradient at each request
    boundary and is freed between requests when the host copy can restore it
    exactly.
    
    - The device partition is freed after the boundary copy only if the host
    gradient restores the running sum bit for bit (same dtype, or an fp32
    host holding bf16/fp16 values). The next backward in the same optimizer
    window restores it. Otherwise (for example bf16 masters with fp32
    accumulation) it stays resident until `step()`.
    - The gate for the compact buffer is unchanged from before this series:
    fp32 accumulation on a 16-bit model, in the stages and offload modes
    that already used it (including stage 1 with offload). Muon groups keep
    the host accumulator. The default bf16/fp16 accumulation keeps the
    per-parameter path, so no partition-sized device buffer is added for it.
    - Overflow is now checked on the value cast to the host gradient dtype.
    With fp16 master weights and fp32 accumulation, an fp32 sum above the
    fp16 range used to pass the check and become inf on the host; it now
    skips the step.
    - Legacy host path: gradients that a non-boundary backward left only in
    the host accumulator are published at the next boundary
    (`_publish_unpublished_offload_grads`).
    - `config.py` is unchanged: fp32 accumulation with fp16/bf16 master
    weights is not rejected, as before.
    - New option `zero_optimization.retain_gpu_grad_partition_until_step`
    (default `false`). The default frees the fp32 gradient partition from
    GPU memory between requests. Set it to `true` to keep the partition in
    GPU memory until `step()`; GPU memory use between requests then rises by
    one partition per rank. With `true`, memory returns to the base level
    and the backward returns to base timing (Qwen3-4B stage 2, 1 GPU: 455 ms
    vs base 474 ms; synthetic: 14.4 ms vs 14.1 ms). Step time is unchanged.
    Test:
    `test_zero_offload_accum_precision.py::TestZeroOffloadReleaseOption`
    checks residency per boundary and that the final weights match in both
    settings.
    
    **Unsupported: bf16 master weights with fp32 gradient accumulation.**
    The host gradient is bf16 and cannot hold the fp32 sum, so the GPU
    partition is not released between requests in that case. It is also
    rounded once to bf16 when copied to the host (see below).
    
    ## Test plan
    
    - CPU: `test_zero2_gradient_safety.py`,
    `test_zero_cpu_offload_grad_accum.py`,
    `test_zero2_offload_multi_backward.py`: 88 passed, 12 skipped. New
    `test_zero_offload_accum_precision.py`: 10 passed.
    - B200 (4 GPUs), final commit `9960ecb7`: targeted offload suites
    (gradient safety, grad-accum norm, multi-backward, coalesced grad
    reduction, config dict) gave 227 passed, 28 warnings; the autoep
    gradient-parity file gave 18 passed, 2 skipped.
    - B200 (4 GPUs), new `test_multiple_request_boundaries_host_accumulator`
    and `test_fp16_host_gradient_overflow_skips_step`: pass. With the
    pre-fix overflow check restored in a scratch copy, the fp32 case of the
    overflow test fails.
    - B200 device-memory probe (single GPU, ZeRO-2 CPU offload, synthetic
    134M-parameter bf16 stack of eight 4096x4096 linears, 3 optimizer
    windows, 4 backwards per window each marked as a request boundary, one
    `step()` per window). Values are MB of `torch.cuda.memory_allocated`
    after each request backward, and the per-window `max_memory_allocated`:
    
    | masters / accumulation | base `a4c989b7`: between requests | this PR
    `9960ecb7`: between requests | window peak, base / this PR |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | fp32 / fp32 | 816 | 304 | 2090 / 2090 |
    | bf16 / fp32 (unsupported) | 816 | 816 | 2090 / 2090 |
    | fp32 / bf16 (default) | 304 | 304 | 1386 / 1386 |
    
    The 512 MB saving between requests is the fp32 partition of this model.
    The in-window peak is unchanged, because the partition is still built
    within a window. Stage 1 and other model sizes were not measured.
    
    ## Test changes
    
    - `test_zero2_gradient_safety.py`: stubs pin the legacy host path with a
    comment; they bypass the reduction that fills the compact buffer.
    - `test_zero_cpu_offload_grad_accum.py`: the norm assertion reads the
    device partition sum, or the host gradient once the partition has been
    freed, and runs with and without fp32 accumulation. It checks every norm
    is above zero.
    - `test_zero2_offload_multi_backward.py`: adds a host-accumulator
    request-boundary test (exact gradient checks; fails if the publish call
    is disabled) and `test_fp16_host_gradient_overflow_skips_step`.
    - `test_zero_offload_accum_precision.py` (new): window-sum precision for
    stage x master x accumulation using micro-step gradients that are exact
    in bf16, and `safe_set_full_grad` residency behavior. See below.
    
    ## Measured precision and residency (not claims about production)
    
    Window sum over 16 micro-steps, relative max error against the exact
    sum, read before `step()`:
    
    | stage | masters | accumulation | error | notes |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | 2 | fp32 | fp32 | 0 | the supported exact case |
    | 2 | fp32 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | per-step bf16 accumulation |
    | 2 | bf16 | fp32 | 2.4e-3 | unsupported: one rounding to the bf16 host
    gradient |
    | 2 | bf16 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | |
    | 1 | fp32 | fp32 | 2.4e-3 | the window sum is copied into the reduction
    bucket of the communication dtype (bf16 here) and rounded once before
    the all-reduce; identical on base |
    | 1 | fp32 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | |
    | 1 | bf16 | fp32 | 2.4e-3 | |
    | 1 | bf16 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | |
    
    The base commit gives the same table, so this PR does not change
    precision for these cells.
    
    Why stage 1 fp32/fp32 is 2.4e-3 and stage 2 fp32/fp32 is 0: stage 2
    reduces each micro-step gradient into the fp32 partition. These
    micro-step values are exact in bf16, so every reduction is exact and the
    fp32 sum is exact. Stage 1 keeps the window sum in fp32 (`grad_accum`),
    but at the boundary it copies that sum into the reduction bucket, which
    has the communication dtype (bf16 in this test, since the model is
    bf16). The sum is therefore rounded once to bf16 before the all-reduce.
    Stage 1 is not changed by this PR. A fp32 reduction for stage 1 would
    remove the rounding at twice the communication volume; it is not in this
    PR.
    
    `safe_set_full_grad` between backwards in one window:
    - A value set while the GPU partition is resident (after the first
    backward of a window) is overwritten at the boundary; it is not kept.
    - A value set after a boundary has freed the partition (fp32 masters) is
    kept, and the next backward accumulates onto it exactly.
    
    ## Stage-1 memory, step time, multi-rank, and Qwen3-4B
    
    Same request-boundary probe as above (every backward is a boundary, then
    `step()`), comparing base `a4c989b7` to this PR. Times are median after
    the first window. Memory is `torch.cuda.memory_allocated` after a
    boundary backward, on rank 0.
    
    **Synthetic 134M-parameter stack (eight 4096x4096 linears), 1 GPU.**
    Between-request memory for fp32 masters + fp32 accumulation drops from
    816 MB to 304 MB on both stage 1 and stage 2. Window peak is unchanged
    (stage 1: 3492 MB; stage 2: 2090 MB). Default bf16 accumulation stays at
    304 MB. Unsupported bf16 masters + fp32 accumulation stays at 816 MB.
    Median `step()` is 26 ms on both trees. Median backward for the released
    fp32-accumulation path is about 10 ms slower on this stack (15→25 ms on
    stage 1, 14→24 ms on stage 2), which is the host copy plus restore on
    the next request. On Qwen3-4B the same path is much slower per backward:
    474→733 ms (stage 2, 1 GPU), 496→785 ms (stage 1, 1 GPU), 483→687 ms
    (stage 2, 2 GPUs). This is the cost of releasing the partition.
    `zero_optimization.retain_gpu_grad_partition_until_step: true` removes
    it, at the price of keeping one fp32 partition resident (see the
    Summary).
    
    **Same stack, 2 GPUs, fp32 masters + fp32 accumulation.** Each rank's
    partition is half the model (256 MB of fp32). Stage 2 between-request
    memory drops from 560 MB to 304 MB; stage 1 from 2468 MB to 2212 MB.
    Window peaks are unchanged. Median `step()` is 127–135 ms on both trees.
    
    **Qwen3-4B (random-init from the published config, 4.02B parameters, seq
    512, 4 request-boundary backwards per window), fp32 masters.**
    
    | stage / GPUs / accumulation | base between (MB) | this PR between (MB)
    | window peak base / this PR (MB) | median step ms base / this PR |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | 2 / 1 / bf16 (default) | 8431 | 8431 | 13251 / 13251 | 3923 / 3782 |
    | 2 / 1 / fp32 | 23775 | 8431 | 29187 / 29187 | 3966 / 3984 |
    | 1 / 1 / bf16 | 8431 | 8431 | 19142 / 19142 | 3899 / 3793 |
    | 1 / 1 / fp32 | 23775 | 8431 | 42182 / 42017 | 3889 / 3929 |
    | 2 / 2 / bf16 | 8431 | 8431 | 13251 / 13251 | 16767 / 16375 |
    | 2 / 2 / fp32 | 16103 | 8431 | 20923 / 20024 | 16176 / 15781 |
    
    On 1 GPU the released fp32 partition is about 15.3 GB (4.02e9 × 4
    bytes). On 2 GPUs it is about 7.7 GB per rank. Default bf16 accumulation
    is unchanged. `step()` is within a few percent of base. This is a
    request-boundary microbenchmark, not a full SFT job.
    
    ## Remaining limits
    
    - No full production training job (loss curve, tokens/s over many steps)
    was run.
    - ZeRO-1 offload with bf16/fp16 masters: fp32 accumulation does
    accumulate in fp32 on the device, but the window sum is rounded once

    ZeRO-1/2: one CPU-offload accumulator per group; zero idle gradients (#9018)
    
    Replacement for #8964, which was closed after an accidental force-push
    of an unrelated commit onto this branch. GitHub will not reopen #8964
    after that rewrite. Follow-up to #8949 (merged as dc046b15). Fixes
    #8991.
    
    This replaces the earlier content of this PR (accumulating every
    backward in the optimizer's FP32 partition gradient). That approach was
    dropped: its extra complexity was not worth its gains. This version
    keeps #8949's design and makes two narrow changes: preallocate the
    CPU-offload accumulator per partition group instead of lazily per
    parameter, and fix the stale-gradient leak.
    
    ## Problem
    
    - **Lazy accumulator complexity.** #8949 stores CPU-offload gradient
    sums in `accumulated_grads_in_cpu`, a dict keyed by parameter id and
    filled on first use. FP32 masters get owned buffers sized to the whole
    parameter; low-precision masters get aliased views of the partition
    gradient, created in two places. Accumulate, copy-back, and restore each
    branch on which kind they hold (about ten branches across four
    functions). The pinned buffers are never unpinned, and the low-precision
    restore leaves stale data in a shared scratch tensor that the overflow
    scan reads.
    - **Stale-gradient leak (#8991).** `reset_cpu_buffers` did not zero the
    FP32 partition gradient. A trainable parameter that receives no gradient
    in the next window kept its previous slice, and Adam applied it again.
    
    ## Fix
    
    - One host accumulator per partition group, sized to the partition, in
    the bit16 dtype, pinned when `cpu_offload_pin_memory` is set. Each
    parameter uses a fixed slice at its `dest_offset`, the same layout as
    the FP32 partition. The buffer is allocated on the first non-boundary
    accumulation, so boundary-only training (GAS=1) pins no extra host
    memory. Low-precision masters keep accumulating in the partition
    gradient.
    - `_get_cpu_offload_accumulator_slice()` is the only place that picks
    the buffer. The per-parameter dict, both alias sites, and the
    full-parameter versus fragment branching are removed.
    - Restore clears the scratch tensor before copying this rank's fragment.
    - The group buffers are unpinned with the other offload buffers.
    - `reset_cpu_buffers` zeros each FP32 partition gradient after the step,
    after overflow, and on reset.
    - `set_norm_for_param_grad` is removed; it has no callers.
    
    No config or API changes.
    
    ## Overflow detection
    
    Restore now zeros the non-owned part of the restored gradient, where
    #8949 kept this rank's local pre-reduction values. Skip-step behavior
    does not change: each reduced fragment is checked by the rank that owns
    it, and `has_overflow()` MAX-reduces `local_overflow` across the
    data-parallel and model-parallel groups. A multi-rank test with an inf
    in a non-owned region was not run.

Author: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 11 00:33:26 2026 +0000

    ZeRO-2 CPU offload: accumulate in the compact partition between requests (#9044)
    
    ## Summary
    
    Follow-up to #9018 (merged as `a4c989b7`). With CPU offload, the compact
    partition-sized accumulator (used for fp32 accumulation on a 16-bit
    model) now publishes to the host partition gradient at each request
    boundary and is freed between requests when the host copy can restore it
    exactly.
    
    - The device partition is freed after the boundary copy only if the host
    gradient restores the running sum bit for bit (same dtype, or an fp32
    host holding bf16/fp16 values). The next backward in the same optimizer
    window restores it. Otherwise (for example bf16 masters with fp32
    accumulation) it stays resident until `step()`.
    - The gate for the compact buffer is unchanged from before this series:
    fp32 accumulation on a 16-bit model, in the stages and offload modes
    that already used it (including stage 1 with offload). Muon groups keep
    the host accumulator. The default bf16/fp16 accumulation keeps the
    per-parameter path, so no partition-sized device buffer is added for it.
    - Overflow is now checked on the value cast to the host gradient dtype.
    With fp16 master weights and fp32 accumulation, an fp32 sum above the
    fp16 range used to pass the check and become inf on the host; it now
    skips the step.
    - Legacy host path: gradients that a non-boundary backward left only in
    the host accumulator are published at the next boundary
    (`_publish_unpublished_offload_grads`).
    - `config.py` is unchanged: fp32 accumulation with fp16/bf16 master
    weights is not rejected, as before.
    - New option `zero_optimization.retain_gpu_grad_partition_until_step`
    (default `false`). The default frees the fp32 gradient partition from
    GPU memory between requests. Set it to `true` to keep the partition in
    GPU memory until `step()`; GPU memory use between requests then rises by
    one partition per rank. With `true`, memory returns to the base level
    and the backward returns to base timing (Qwen3-4B stage 2, 1 GPU: 455 ms
    vs base 474 ms; synthetic: 14.4 ms vs 14.1 ms). Step time is unchanged.
    Test:
    `test_zero_offload_accum_precision.py::TestZeroOffloadReleaseOption`
    checks residency per boundary and that the final weights match in both
    settings.
    
    **Unsupported: bf16 master weights with fp32 gradient accumulation.**
    The host gradient is bf16 and cannot hold the fp32 sum, so the GPU
    partition is not released between requests in that case. It is also
    rounded once to bf16 when copied to the host (see below).
    
    ## Test plan
    
    - CPU: `test_zero2_gradient_safety.py`,
    `test_zero_cpu_offload_grad_accum.py`,
    `test_zero2_offload_multi_backward.py`: 88 passed, 12 skipped. New
    `test_zero_offload_accum_precision.py`: 10 passed.
    - B200 (4 GPUs), final commit `9960ecb7`: targeted offload suites
    (gradient safety, grad-accum norm, multi-backward, coalesced grad
    reduction, config dict) gave 227 passed, 28 warnings; the autoep
    gradient-parity file gave 18 passed, 2 skipped.
    - B200 (4 GPUs), new `test_multiple_request_boundaries_host_accumulator`
    and `test_fp16_host_gradient_overflow_skips_step`: pass. With the
    pre-fix overflow check restored in a scratch copy, the fp32 case of the
    overflow test fails.
    - B200 device-memory probe (single GPU, ZeRO-2 CPU offload, synthetic
    134M-parameter bf16 stack of eight 4096x4096 linears, 3 optimizer
    windows, 4 backwards per window each marked as a request boundary, one
    `step()` per window). Values are MB of `torch.cuda.memory_allocated`
    after each request backward, and the per-window `max_memory_allocated`:
    
    | masters / accumulation | base `a4c989b7`: between requests | this PR
    `9960ecb7`: between requests | window peak, base / this PR |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | fp32 / fp32 | 816 | 304 | 2090 / 2090 |
    | bf16 / fp32 (unsupported) | 816 | 816 | 2090 / 2090 |
    | fp32 / bf16 (default) | 304 | 304 | 1386 / 1386 |
    
    The 512 MB saving between requests is the fp32 partition of this model.
    The in-window peak is unchanged, because the partition is still built
    within a window. Stage 1 and other model sizes were not measured.
    
    ## Test changes
    
    - `test_zero2_gradient_safety.py`: stubs pin the legacy host path with a
    comment; they bypass the reduction that fills the compact buffer.
    - `test_zero_cpu_offload_grad_accum.py`: the norm assertion reads the
    device partition sum, or the host gradient once the partition has been
    freed, and runs with and without fp32 accumulation. It checks every norm
    is above zero.
    - `test_zero2_offload_multi_backward.py`: adds a host-accumulator
    request-boundary test (exact gradient checks; fails if the publish call
    is disabled) and `test_fp16_host_gradient_overflow_skips_step`.
    - `test_zero_offload_accum_precision.py` (new): window-sum precision for
    stage x master x accumulation using micro-step gradients that are exact
    in bf16, and `safe_set_full_grad` residency behavior. See below.
    
    ## Measured precision and residency (not claims about production)
    
    Window sum over 16 micro-steps, relative max error against the exact
    sum, read before `step()`:
    
    | stage | masters | accumulation | error | notes |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | 2 | fp32 | fp32 | 0 | the supported exact case |
    | 2 | fp32 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | per-step bf16 accumulation |
    | 2 | bf16 | fp32 | 2.4e-3 | unsupported: one rounding to the bf16 host
    gradient |
    | 2 | bf16 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | |
    | 1 | fp32 | fp32 | 2.4e-3 | the window sum is copied into the reduction
    bucket of the communication dtype (bf16 here) and rounded once before
    the all-reduce; identical on base |
    | 1 | fp32 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | |
    | 1 | bf16 | fp32 | 2.4e-3 | |
    | 1 | bf16 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | |
    
    The base commit gives the same table, so this PR does not change
    precision for these cells.
    
    Why stage 1 fp32/fp32 is 2.4e-3 and stage 2 fp32/fp32 is 0: stage 2
    reduces each micro-step gradient into the fp32 partition. These
    micro-step values are exact in bf16, so every reduction is exact and the
    fp32 sum is exact. Stage 1 keeps the window sum in fp32 (`grad_accum`),
    but at the boundary it copies that sum into the reduction bucket, which
    has the communication dtype (bf16 in this test, since the model is
    bf16). The sum is therefore rounded once to bf16 before the all-reduce.
    Stage 1 is not changed by this PR. A fp32 reduction for stage 1 would
    remove the rounding at twice the communication volume; it is not in this
    PR.
    
    `safe_set_full_grad` between backwards in one window:
    - A value set while the GPU partition is resident (after the first
    backward of a window) is overwritten at the boundary; it is not kept.
    - A value set after a boundary has freed the partition (fp32 masters) is
    kept, and the next backward accumulates onto it exactly.
    
    ## Stage-1 memory, step time, multi-rank, and Qwen3-4B
    
    Same request-boundary probe as above (every backward is a boundary, then
    `step()`), comparing base `a4c989b7` to this PR. Times are median after
    the first window. Memory is `torch.cuda.memory_allocated` after a
    boundary backward, on rank 0.
    
    **Synthetic 134M-parameter stack (eight 4096x4096 linears), 1 GPU.**
    Between-request memory for fp32 masters + fp32 accumulation drops from
    816 MB to 304 MB on both stage 1 and stage 2. Window peak is unchanged
    (stage 1: 3492 MB; stage 2: 2090 MB). Default bf16 accumulation stays at
    304 MB. Unsupported bf16 masters + fp32 accumulation stays at 816 MB.
    Median `step()` is 26 ms on both trees. Median backward for the released
    fp32-accumulation path is about 10 ms slower on this stack (15→25 ms on
    stage 1, 14→24 ms on stage 2), which is the host copy plus restore on
    the next request. On Qwen3-4B the same path is much slower per backward:
    474→733 ms (stage 2, 1 GPU), 496→785 ms (stage 1, 1 GPU), 483→687 ms
    (stage 2, 2 GPUs). This is the cost of releasing the partition.
    `zero_optimization.retain_gpu_grad_partition_until_step: true` removes
    it, at the price of keeping one fp32 partition resident (see the
    Summary).
    
    **Same stack, 2 GPUs, fp32 masters + fp32 accumulation.** Each rank's
    partition is half the model (256 MB of fp32). Stage 2 between-request
    memory drops from 560 MB to 304 MB; stage 1 from 2468 MB to 2212 MB.
    Window peaks are unchanged. Median `step()` is 127–135 ms on both trees.
    
    **Qwen3-4B (random-init from the published config, 4.02B parameters, seq
    512, 4 request-boundary backwards per window), fp32 masters.**
    
    | stage / GPUs / accumulation | base between (MB) | this PR between (MB)
    | window peak base / this PR (MB) | median step ms base / this PR |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | 2 / 1 / bf16 (default) | 8431 | 8431 | 13251 / 13251 | 3923 / 3782 |
    | 2 / 1 / fp32 | 23775 | 8431 | 29187 / 29187 | 3966 / 3984 |
    | 1 / 1 / bf16 | 8431 | 8431 | 19142 / 19142 | 3899 / 3793 |
    | 1 / 1 / fp32 | 23775 | 8431 | 42182 / 42017 | 3889 / 3929 |
    | 2 / 2 / bf16 | 8431 | 8431 | 13251 / 13251 | 16767 / 16375 |
    | 2 / 2 / fp32 | 16103 | 8431 | 20923 / 20024 | 16176 / 15781 |
    
    On 1 GPU the released fp32 partition is about 15.3 GB (4.02e9 × 4
    bytes). On 2 GPUs it is about 7.7 GB per rank. Default bf16 accumulation
    is unchanged. `step()` is within a few percent of base. This is a
    request-boundary microbenchmark, not a full SFT job.

    - ZeRO-1 offload with bf16/fp16 masters: fp32 accumulation does
    accumulate in fp32 on the device, but the window sum is rounded once

    [VocabTP] Add vocabulary-parallel generalized JSD with Triton kernels (#8958)
    
    ## Motivation
    
    Teacher-student training compares the models' next-token distributions,
    not
    just the probability of a single ground-truth token. DeepSpeed already
    offers
    vocabulary-parallel forward/reverse KL, but does not support the
    interior
    `0 < beta < 1` generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence used by GKD-style
    distillation. Applying a local softmax independently on each vocabulary
    shard
    does not compute the intended full-vocabulary objective.
    
    TRL currently has two relevant implementations on its main branch:
    `experimental.GKDTrainer` computes generalized JSD from materialized
    logits;
    `DistillationTrainer` uses completion filtering and tiled LM-head
    projection
    to compute KL/JSD without materializing full logits. Those
    implementations do
    not call DeepSpeed's vocabulary-parallel divergence ops. In particular,
    support for DeepSpeed/ZeRO or FSDP parameter sharding is not itself
    support
    for a vocabulary-parallel softmax and divergence.
    
    This PR supplies the missing Core logits-based primitive, as a building
    block
    for teacher-student workloads and a possible subsequent TRL integration.
    It
    does not claim to integrate TRL or replace its memory-efficient tiled
    loss.
    Refs #8790.
    
    ## Changes
    
    - Add `vocab_parallel_jsd(student_logits, teacher_logits, beta=0.5,
    tp_group=None)`, returning FP32 per-token divergence replicated on TP
    ranks.
    - Add fused Triton paired softmax statistics, divergence and backward
    kernels.
    Reuse global normalization and reduce the two KL-to-mixture expectations
    together. Recompute probabilities in registers during backward rather
    than
    retaining full FP32 probability tensors; keep bounded eager chunks as
    fallback.
    - Enable JSD on an active Intel Triton backend without changing XPU's
    global
      Triton capability flag or existing-op dispatch.
    - Support gradients to both inputs, detached teachers, uneven vocabulary
      shards, empty local shards, and non-contiguous causal-shift views.
    - Preserve the existing Core convention: beta=0 selects forward KL and
    beta=1
    selects reverse KL. These are explicit endpoint branches, not continuous
      limits of the weighted interior JSD.
    - Leave temperature, optional T-squared scaling, masking and
    normalization to
      the caller, following the existing vocabulary-parallel per-token ops.
    
    ## Not a duplicate
    
    - #8791 / #8838 implement logprobs, entropy and forward/reverse KL, not
      interior-beta generalized JSD. The new API reuses their KL endpoints.
    - #8947 fixes counting and accumulation in the existing dense rollout
    loss.
      This PR does not edit `runtime/rollout/opsd.py` or its tests.
    - DeepSpeedExamples#1019 integrates vocabulary-parallel KL into OPSD.
    This PR
    does not change Examples, cache handling, rollout or trainer
    integration.
    - #8945 connects fused-linear CE to HF forward. This PR is independent
    of it:
      no LM-head projection changes or loss-function hooks.
    
    ## Scope and limitations
    
    This is a new opt-in logits-based API; existing ops and training
    defaults are
    unchanged. Unlike the existing single-pass KL forward, JSD needs global
    normalization before evaluating the nonlinear mixture: statistics and
    divergence are two input passes. It still consumes materialized local
    logits.
    Top-k restriction, pointwise
    clipping, differing student/teacher shard layouts, fused-linear
    divergence,
    DeepCompile support and automatic TRL integration are not included.
    
    Every TP rank must supply identically ordered student/teacher vocabulary
    shards and backpropagate the same replicated per-token loss.
    
    ## Validation
    
    Hardware: up to 4 Intel Arc Pro B70 GPUs, XCCL, driver 1.15.39122+11,
    torch 2.14.0.dev20260804+xpu, Intel Triton 3.8.0. Final validation: **67
    CPU
    regressions passed, 11 fused XPU cases passed, and 4 distributed cases
    passed
    at each of TP1/2/4**. Existing entropy/KL Triton-only tests still skip
    on XPU
    because their accelerator-wide flag remains disabled; JSD uses its own
    checked
    Intel backend dispatch. The final TP cases cover FP32/BF16 interior JSD
    versus
    an FP64 oracle, empty shards/disjoint support, and head SGD update
    parity.
    
    On NVIDIA L20, driver 580.173.02, torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0),
    Triton 3.8.0, NCCL: the **full test file passed, 113 passed with no
    skips**.
    This includes all JSD TP1/2/4 cases and FP32/FP16/BF16 single-device
    kernels.
    The existing `ds` conda environment was used without dependency changes;
    tested source hashes match the local implementation and tests.
    
    ```bash
    PYTHONPATH=tests:. OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 pytest \
      tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py -q \
      -k 'not TestVocabParallel and not triton'
    PYTHONPATH=tests:. OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 pytest \
      tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py -q -k jsd_triton
    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 PYTHONPATH=tests:. \
      pytest --forked tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py -q \
      -k 'TestVocabParallelJSDTP and (0.2 or empty or optimizer)'
    pre-commit run --files deepspeed/ops/triton_ops/vocab_parallel_softmax.py \
      deepspeed/sequence/vocab_parallel_ops.py \
      tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py \
      docs/_tutorials/autotp-training.md
    git diff --check
    # L20 full-file run:
    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 PYTHONPATH=tests:. OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 \
      pytest --forked tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py \
      -q --color=no
    ```
    
    Scoped pre-commit hooks and diff checks pass. Numerical checks use an
    independent FP64 dense PyTorch reference, nonuniform vocabulary
    partitions,
    FP32/BF16, both-input gradients and frozen inputs. Additional cases
    cover
    disjoint support, undefined masked rows, empty local shards, empty token
    batches, causal-shift views, independent large logit shifts and row
    chunking.
    Three SGD updates of a sharded head match the dense reference at
    TP1/2/4.
    This head-only training test does not exercise a DeepSpeed Engine or
    ZeRO.

    | TP | Implementation | Peak allocated GiB/rank | Time ms, median |
    |---|---|---:|---:|
    | 2 | Gather both logits, dense PyTorch JSD | 6.671 | 112.17 |
    | 2 | Vocabulary-parallel eager JSD | 1.057 | 58.38 |
    | 2 | Vocabulary-parallel Triton JSD | 0.435 | 3.08 |
    | 2 | Existing Triton reverse KL | 0.435 | 3.29 |

    | 4 | Vocabulary-parallel Triton JSD | 0.217 | 3.41 |
    | 4 | Existing Triton reverse KL | 0.217 | 3.16 |
    
    Five warmups and ten measured trials, synchronized wall time; per-trial
    MAX
    over TP ranks, independently for time and memory. Resident input
    allocations
    are included in peak. Student gradients are included. All arms start
    with sharded logits, and the dense arm includes
    their gather; it is not TRL's existing chunked-projection
    implementation.
    Losses and local student gradients match before timing. Clocks were not
    pinned. This benchmark excludes head projection, backbone, optimizer and
    rollout; it demonstrates only an op-level comparison, not full-training
    or
    TRL speedup. Reproduction script and raw JSON/logs are retained locally
    and
    should be attached to the PR when submitted. KL's Triton kernels are
    enabled
    only in the XPU benchmark for comparison; their production dispatch is
    unchanged.

    | TP | Implementation | Peak allocated GiB/rank | Time ms, median |
    |---|---|---:|---:|
    | 2 | Gather both logits, dense PyTorch JSD | 6.671 | 98.02 |

    L20 clocks were also not pinned; these remain exploratory op-level

    All 15 CUDA sm89 offline kernel compilations pass (FP32/FP16/BF16 and

    student-only/teacher-only backward variants), in addition to the actual

    runtime validation above.
    
    Not validated: ZeRO stages, offload, PP/SP,

    Persist ZeRO-3 HybridMegatron QKV layout changes (#8392)
    
    ## Summary
    
    - persist GPT-NeoX/Megatron QKV inference-layout mutations when ZeRO-3
    repartitions gathered parameters
    - persist the inverse layout mutation when returning to training
    - add a focused QKV layout round-trip regression test
    
    `GatheredParameters` needs `modifier_rank` when a gathered full
    parameter is modified. Without it, the transformed QKV tensor is not
    reliably broadcast before repartitioning, and the inference operator can
    interpret the original head-interleaved GPT-NeoX layout as contiguous
    Q/K/V.
    
    Closes #8391.

    together. Recompute probabilities in registers during backward rather

Author: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>
Date:   Mon Nov 9 02:17:20 2026 +0000

    ZeRO-1/2: one CPU-offload accumulator per group; zero idle gradients (#9018)
    
    Replacement for #8964, which was closed after an accidental force-push
    of an unrelated commit onto this branch. GitHub will not reopen #8964
    after that rewrite. Follow-up to #8949 (merged as dc046b15). Fixes
    #8991.
    
    This replaces the earlier content of this PR (accumulating every
    backward in the optimizer's FP32 partition gradient). That approach was
    dropped: its extra complexity was not worth its gains. This version
    keeps #8949's design and makes two narrow changes: preallocate the
    CPU-offload accumulator per partition group instead of lazily per
    parameter, and fix the stale-gradient leak.
    
    ## Problem
    
    - **Lazy accumulator complexity.** #8949 stores CPU-offload gradient
    sums in `accumulated_grads_in_cpu`, a dict keyed by parameter id and
    filled on first use. FP32 masters get owned buffers sized to the whole
    parameter; low-precision masters get aliased views of the partition
    gradient, created in two places. Accumulate, copy-back, and restore each
    branch on which kind they hold (about ten branches across four
    functions). The pinned buffers are never unpinned, and the low-precision
    restore leaves stale data in a shared scratch tensor that the overflow
    scan reads.
    - **Stale-gradient leak (#8991).** `reset_cpu_buffers` did not zero the
    FP32 partition gradient. A trainable parameter that receives no gradient
    in the next window kept its previous slice, and Adam applied it again.
    
    ## Fix
    
    - One host accumulator per partition group, sized to the partition, in
    the bit16 dtype, pinned when `cpu_offload_pin_memory` is set. Each
    parameter uses a fixed slice at its `dest_offset`, the same layout as
    the FP32 partition. The buffer is allocated on the first non-boundary
    accumulation, so boundary-only training (GAS=1) pins no extra host
    memory. Low-precision masters keep accumulating in the partition
    gradient.
    - `_get_cpu_offload_accumulator_slice()` is the only place that picks
    the buffer. The per-parameter dict, both alias sites, and the
    full-parameter versus fragment branching are removed.
    - Restore clears the scratch tensor before copying this rank's fragment.
    - The group buffers are unpinned with the other offload buffers.
    - `reset_cpu_buffers` zeros each FP32 partition gradient after the step,
    after overflow, and on reset.
    - `set_norm_for_param_grad` is removed; it has no callers.
    
    No config or API changes.
    
    ## Overflow detection
    
    Restore now zeros the non-owned part of the restored gradient, where
    #8949 kept this rank's local pre-reduction values. Skip-step behavior
    does not change: each reduced fragment is checked by the rank that owns
    it, and `has_overflow()` MAX-reduces `local_overflow` across the
    data-parallel and model-parallel groups. A multi-rank test with an inf
    in a non-owned region was not run.
    
    ## Not a duplicate
    
    - #8949 (merged): this builds on it.
    - #8991 (open issue): the leak this fixes.
    - #8728 (merged as 0d0aa30b): clears stale offload scratch before
    restoring low-precision gradients. Its change is the same `zero_()` in
    `_restore_cpu_offload_grad_to_gpu` that this PR includes. This PR is
    rebased onto master (b62afa82) after #8728 landed. The one conflict was
    in `_restore_cpu_offload_grad_to_gpu`; the resolution keeps this PR's
    version (unconditional `zero_()` on the scratch, then the fragment copy
    from `_get_cpu_offload_accumulator_slice`).
    - #8920 (open): FP32 folded-gradient accumulation. Unrelated.
    - #8957 (open issue): remaining test coverage. Not required for this
    change.
    
    ## Validation
    
    ### CPU unit tests
    
    Hardware: 1x Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C (96 logical CPUs), no GPU. Python
    3.12.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu130.
    
    ```bash
    python -m pytest -q tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero2_gradient_safety.py \

    `test_zero_cpu_offload_grad_accum.py`, and
    `test_zero2_offload_multi_backward.py` (includes #8728's test) run with

    #8728's regression test,
    `TestZero2OffloadOverflowRecovery::test_finite_step_after_overflow` (two
    CPU ranks via `LOCAL_SIZE=2`, BF16 and FP16, low-precision and FP32
    masters), passes 4/4 on this branch. With the `zero_()` in

    (`test_idle_parameter_window_does_not_reuse_previous_gradient`,
    `test_idle_parameter_stays_zero_beside_active_neighbor`, FP32 and BF16
    masters) compare against `torch.optim.Adam`; all four fail with the
    `reset_cpu_buffers` zeroing removed.
    `test_single_boundary_offload_avoids_auxiliary_storage_and_copy` checks

      tests/unit/runtime/zero/test_zero1_optimizer_fastpath.py \
      tests/unit/runtime/half_precision/test_zero_grad_norm_overflow.py

    ZeRO-2 CPU offload: accumulate in the compact partition between requests (#9044)
    
    ## Summary
    
    Follow-up to #9018 (merged as `a4c989b7`). With CPU offload, the compact
    partition-sized accumulator (used for fp32 accumulation on a 16-bit
    model) now publishes to the host partition gradient at each request
    boundary and is freed between requests when the host copy can restore it
    exactly.
    
    - The device partition is freed after the boundary copy only if the host
    gradient restores the running sum bit for bit (same dtype, or an fp32
    host holding bf16/fp16 values). The next backward in the same optimizer
    window restores it. Otherwise (for example bf16 masters with fp32
    accumulation) it stays resident until `step()`.
    - The gate for the compact buffer is unchanged from before this series:
    fp32 accumulation on a 16-bit model, in the stages and offload modes
    that already used it (including stage 1 with offload). Muon groups keep
    the host accumulator. The default bf16/fp16 accumulation keeps the
    per-parameter path, so no partition-sized device buffer is added for it.
    - Overflow is now checked on the value cast to the host gradient dtype.
    With fp16 master weights and fp32 accumulation, an fp32 sum above the
    fp16 range used to pass the check and become inf on the host; it now
    skips the step.
    - Legacy host path: gradients that a non-boundary backward left only in
    the host accumulator are published at the next boundary
    (`_publish_unpublished_offload_grads`).
    - `config.py` is unchanged: fp32 accumulation with fp16/bf16 master
    weights is not rejected, as before.
    - New option `zero_optimization.retain_gpu_grad_partition_until_step`
    (default `false`). The default frees the fp32 gradient partition from
    GPU memory between requests. Set it to `true` to keep the partition in
    GPU memory until `step()`; GPU memory use between requests then rises by
    one partition per rank. With `true`, memory returns to the base level
    and the backward returns to base timing (Qwen3-4B stage 2, 1 GPU: 455 ms
    vs base 474 ms; synthetic: 14.4 ms vs 14.1 ms). Step time is unchanged.
    Test:
    `test_zero_offload_accum_precision.py::TestZeroOffloadReleaseOption`
    checks residency per boundary and that the final weights match in both
    settings.
    
    **Unsupported: bf16 master weights with fp32 gradient accumulation.**
    The host gradient is bf16 and cannot hold the fp32 sum, so the GPU
    partition is not released between requests in that case. It is also
    rounded once to bf16 when copied to the host (see below).
    
    ## Test plan
    
    - CPU: `test_zero2_gradient_safety.py`,
    `test_zero_cpu_offload_grad_accum.py`,
    `test_zero2_offload_multi_backward.py`: 88 passed, 12 skipped. New
    `test_zero_offload_accum_precision.py`: 10 passed.
    - B200 (4 GPUs), final commit `9960ecb7`: targeted offload suites
    (gradient safety, grad-accum norm, multi-backward, coalesced grad
    reduction, config dict) gave 227 passed, 28 warnings; the autoep
    gradient-parity file gave 18 passed, 2 skipped.
    - B200 (4 GPUs), new `test_multiple_request_boundaries_host_accumulator`
    and `test_fp16_host_gradient_overflow_skips_step`: pass. With the
    pre-fix overflow check restored in a scratch copy, the fp32 case of the
    overflow test fails.
    - B200 device-memory probe (single GPU, ZeRO-2 CPU offload, synthetic
    134M-parameter bf16 stack of eight 4096x4096 linears, 3 optimizer
    windows, 4 backwards per window each marked as a request boundary, one
    `step()` per window). Values are MB of `torch.cuda.memory_allocated`
    after each request backward, and the per-window `max_memory_allocated`:
    
    | masters / accumulation | base `a4c989b7`: between requests | this PR
    `9960ecb7`: between requests | window peak, base / this PR |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | fp32 / fp32 | 816 | 304 | 2090 / 2090 |
    | bf16 / fp32 (unsupported) | 816 | 816 | 2090 / 2090 |
    | fp32 / bf16 (default) | 304 | 304 | 1386 / 1386 |
    
    The 512 MB saving between requests is the fp32 partition of this model.
    The in-window peak is unchanged, because the partition is still built
    within a window. Stage 1 and other model sizes were not measured.
    
    ## Test changes
    
    - `test_zero2_gradient_safety.py`: stubs pin the legacy host path with a
    comment; they bypass the reduction that fills the compact buffer.
    - `test_zero_cpu_offload_grad_accum.py`: the norm assertion reads the
    device partition sum, or the host gradient once the partition has been
    freed, and runs with and without fp32 accumulation. It checks every norm
    is above zero.
    - `test_zero2_offload_multi_backward.py`: adds a host-accumulator
    request-boundary test (exact gradient checks; fails if the publish call
    is disabled) and `test_fp16_host_gradient_overflow_skips_step`.
    - `test_zero_offload_accum_precision.py` (new): window-sum precision for
    stage x master x accumulation using micro-step gradients that are exact
    in bf16, and `safe_set_full_grad` residency behavior. See below.
    
    ## Measured precision and residency (not claims about production)
    
    Window sum over 16 micro-steps, relative max error against the exact
    sum, read before `step()`:
    
    | stage | masters | accumulation | error | notes |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | 2 | fp32 | fp32 | 0 | the supported exact case |
    | 2 | fp32 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | per-step bf16 accumulation |
    | 2 | bf16 | fp32 | 2.4e-3 | unsupported: one rounding to the bf16 host
    gradient |
    | 2 | bf16 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | |
    | 1 | fp32 | fp32 | 2.4e-3 | the window sum is copied into the reduction
    bucket of the communication dtype (bf16 here) and rounded once before
    the all-reduce; identical on base |
    | 1 | fp32 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | |
    | 1 | bf16 | fp32 | 2.4e-3 | |
    | 1 | bf16 | bf16 | 6.2e-3 | |
    
    The base commit gives the same table, so this PR does not change
    precision for these cells.
    
    Why stage 1 fp32/fp32 is 2.4e-3 and stage 2 fp32/fp32 is 0: stage 2
    reduces each micro-step gradient into the fp32 partition. These
    micro-step values are exact in bf16, so every reduction is exact and the
    fp32 sum is exact. Stage 1 keeps the window sum in fp32 (`grad_accum`),
    but at the boundary it copies that sum into the reduction bucket, which
    has the communication dtype (bf16 in this test, since the model is
    bf16). The sum is therefore rounded once to bf16 before the all-reduce.
    Stage 1 is not changed by this PR. A fp32 reduction for stage 1 would
    remove the rounding at twice the communication volume; it is not in this
    PR.
    
    `safe_set_full_grad` between backwards in one window:
    - A value set while the GPU partition is resident (after the first
    backward of a window) is overwritten at the boundary; it is not kept.
    - A value set after a boundary has freed the partition (fp32 masters) is
    kept, and the next backward accumulates onto it exactly.
    
    ## Stage-1 memory, step time, multi-rank, and Qwen3-4B
    
    Same request-boundary probe as above (every backward is a boundary, then
    `step()`), comparing base `a4c989b7` to this PR. Times are median after
    the first window. Memory is `torch.cuda.memory_allocated` after a
    boundary backward, on rank 0.

    Between-request memory for fp32 masters + fp32 accumulation drops from
    816 MB to 304 MB on both stage 1 and stage 2. Window peak is unchanged
    (stage 1: 3492 MB; stage 2: 2090 MB). Default bf16 accumulation stays at
    304 MB. Unsupported bf16 masters + fp32 accumulation stays at 816 MB.
    Median `step()` is 26 ms on both trees. Median backward for the released
    fp32-accumulation path is about 10 ms slower on this stack (15→25 ms on

    474→733 ms (stage 2, 1 GPU), 496→785 ms (stage 1, 1 GPU), 483→687 ms

    `zero_optimization.retain_gpu_grad_partition_until_step: true` removes
    it, at the price of keeping one fp32 partition resident (see the

    **Same stack, 2 GPUs, fp32 masters + fp32 accumulation.** Each rank's

    **Qwen3-4B (random-init from the published config, 4.02B parameters, seq

    | stage / GPUs / accumulation | base between (MB) | this PR between (MB)

    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | 2 / 1 / bf16 (default) | 8431 | 8431 | 13251 / 13251 | 3923 / 3782 |

    [VocabTP] Add vocabulary-parallel generalized JSD with Triton kernels (#8958)
    
    ## Motivation
    
    Teacher-student training compares the models' next-token distributions,
    not
    just the probability of a single ground-truth token. DeepSpeed already
    offers
    vocabulary-parallel forward/reverse KL, but does not support the
    interior
    `0 < beta < 1` generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence used by GKD-style
    distillation. Applying a local softmax independently on each vocabulary
    shard
    does not compute the intended full-vocabulary objective.
    
    TRL currently has two relevant implementations on its main branch:
    `experimental.GKDTrainer` computes generalized JSD from materialized
    logits;
    `DistillationTrainer` uses completion filtering and tiled LM-head
    projection
    to compute KL/JSD without materializing full logits. Those
    implementations do
    not call DeepSpeed's vocabulary-parallel divergence ops. In particular,
    support for DeepSpeed/ZeRO or FSDP parameter sharding is not itself
    support
    for a vocabulary-parallel softmax and divergence.
    
    This PR supplies the missing Core logits-based primitive, as a building
    block
    for teacher-student workloads and a possible subsequent TRL integration.
    It
    does not claim to integrate TRL or replace its memory-efficient tiled
    loss.
    Refs #8790.
    
    ## Changes
    
    - Add `vocab_parallel_jsd(student_logits, teacher_logits, beta=0.5,
    tp_group=None)`, returning FP32 per-token divergence replicated on TP
    ranks.
    - Add fused Triton paired softmax statistics, divergence and backward
    kernels.
    Reuse global normalization and reduce the two KL-to-mixture expectations
    together. Recompute probabilities in registers during backward rather
    than
    retaining full FP32 probability tensors; keep bounded eager chunks as
    fallback.
    - Enable JSD on an active Intel Triton backend without changing XPU's
    global
      Triton capability flag or existing-op dispatch.
    - Support gradients to both inputs, detached teachers, uneven vocabulary
      shards, empty local shards, and non-contiguous causal-shift views.
    - Preserve the existing Core convention: beta=0 selects forward KL and
    beta=1
    selects reverse KL. These are explicit endpoint branches, not continuous
      limits of the weighted interior JSD.
    - Leave temperature, optional T-squared scaling, masking and
    normalization to
      the caller, following the existing vocabulary-parallel per-token ops.
    
    ## Not a duplicate
    
    - #8791 / #8838 implement logprobs, entropy and forward/reverse KL, not
      interior-beta generalized JSD. The new API reuses their KL endpoints.
    - #8947 fixes counting and accumulation in the existing dense rollout
    loss.
      This PR does not edit `runtime/rollout/opsd.py` or its tests.
    - DeepSpeedExamples#1019 integrates vocabulary-parallel KL into OPSD.
    This PR
    does not change Examples, cache handling, rollout or trainer
    integration.
    - #8945 connects fused-linear CE to HF forward. This PR is independent
    of it:
      no LM-head projection changes or loss-function hooks.
    
    ## Scope and limitations
    
    This is a new opt-in logits-based API; existing ops and training
    defaults are
    unchanged. Unlike the existing single-pass KL forward, JSD needs global
    normalization before evaluating the nonlinear mixture: statistics and
    divergence are two input passes. It still consumes materialized local
    logits.
    Top-k restriction, pointwise
    clipping, differing student/teacher shard layouts, fused-linear
    divergence,
    DeepCompile support and automatic TRL integration are not included.
    
    Every TP rank must supply identically ordered student/teacher vocabulary
    shards and backpropagate the same replicated per-token loss.
    
    ## Validation
    
    Hardware: up to 4 Intel Arc Pro B70 GPUs, XCCL, driver 1.15.39122+11,
    torch 2.14.0.dev20260804+xpu, Intel Triton 3.8.0. Final validation: **67
    CPU
    regressions passed, 11 fused XPU cases passed, and 4 distributed cases
    passed
    at each of TP1/2/4**. Existing entropy/KL Triton-only tests still skip
    on XPU
    because their accelerator-wide flag remains disabled; JSD uses its own
    checked
    Intel backend dispatch. The final TP cases cover FP32/BF16 interior JSD
    versus
    an FP64 oracle, empty shards/disjoint support, and head SGD update
    parity.
    
    On NVIDIA L20, driver 580.173.02, torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0),
    Triton 3.8.0, NCCL: the **full test file passed, 113 passed with no
    skips**.
    This includes all JSD TP1/2/4 cases and FP32/FP16/BF16 single-device
    kernels.
    The existing `ds` conda environment was used without dependency changes;
    tested source hashes match the local implementation and tests.

    Persist ZeRO-3 HybridMegatron QKV layout changes (#8392)
    
    ## Summary
    
    - persist GPT-NeoX/Megatron QKV inference-layout mutations when ZeRO-3
    repartitions gathered parameters
    - persist the inverse layout mutation when returning to training
    - add a focused QKV layout round-trip regression test
    
    `GatheredParameters` needs `modifier_rank` when a gathered full
    parameter is modified. Without it, the transformed QKV tensor is not
    reliably broadcast before repartitioning, and the inference operator can
    interpret the original head-interleaved GPT-NeoX layout as contiguous
    Q/K/V.

    `max_abs=0`; native and HE first token both `187`
    - 20-step Pythia HE training completed on 2 x MI250, 8 x MI250, and 8 x
    MI300X without layout-round-trip recurrence
    
    ## Scope
    
    This PR intentionally contains only the ZeRO-3 QKV mutation-persistence
    fix. A separate compatibility issue in recent Transformers
    (`GPTNeoXAttention.hidden_size` removal) can prevent current master from
    reaching injection in that environment and is not bundled here.

commit f32e164b947dcf681910e4c3d839870072f050ee
Author: Hongwei Chen <33092912+hwchen2017@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Mon Nov 9 13:17:04 2026 +0000

    Fix memory leak in engine and zero optimizer (#9034)
    
    Fixes #7204 (ZeRO-3 + CPU offload, host RAM grows every time the engine
    is destroyed and re-initialized).
    
    ## Problem
    `engine.destroy()` does not release the engine: after `destroy()`, `del`
    and `gc.collect()`, the engine and its optimizer stay reachable, so
    every re-initialization causes memory leak. Each create → train →
    `destroy()` → `del` → `gc.collect()` cycle leaks the whole engine and
    optimizer: about 2 GiB of GPU memory per cycle on the repro model below,
    or about 4 GiB of host RAM per cycle with CPU offload (the #7204 setup).
    ZeRO-3 leaks even when the caller drops the model. ZeRO-0/1/2 and
    `BF16_Optimizer` leak when the caller keeps the model,
    as HF Trainer does. This PR removes the references that keep a destroyed
    engine alive, so its memory is freed while the caller still holds the
    model.
    
    ## Root cause and fixes
    
    A referrer-chain search from the destroyed engine back to GC roots found
    references 1-5. Items 6 and 7 came from the
    re-wrap and other-optimizer checks under Validation.
    
    1. **Engine forward hooks** (`engine.py`): the forward pre/post hooks
    and `first_dataloader_check` stay registered on the model. `destroy()`
    now removes them, after `_deactivate_deepcompile()`, which re-registers
    the forward hooks.
    2. **`FWD_MODULE_STACK`** (`parameter_offload.py`): ZeRO-3 pushes the
    top module onto this process-wide list and never
    pops it. `DeepSpeedZeRoOffload.destroy()` now removes its entry, at most
    once per instance
    (`_has_fwd_stack_entry`), so destroying a replaced engine a second time
    cannot remove the entry of a newer engine that
       wraps the same model.
    3. **Class-level `functools.lru_cache`** on
    `PartitionedParameterCoordinator.__params_to_release`: the cache keys on
    `self` and is never cleared, so it keeps every coordinator and its
    modules alive. The cache is now created per
    instance in `__init__`, with the same key and the same never-invalidated
    behavior.
    4. **`p._z3_optimizer`** (`stage3.py`): cleared in `destroy()` when it
    points at this optimizer.
    5. **`lp._zero_optimizer`** (`stage_1_and_2.py`, ZeRO-1/2 with CPU
    offload): deleted in `destroy()` when it points at
       this optimizer.
    6. **Second teardown at garbage collection** (`engine.py`): once 1-5
    make a destroyed engine collectable,
    `DeepSpeedEngine.__del__` would run `destroy()` again. If a newer engine
    already wraps the same model, that second
    teardown resets the newer engine's `_hp_mapping` (ZeRO-1/2 and
    `BF16_Optimizer`: `safe_get_full_fp32_param` then
    returns zeros) and its `FWD_MODULE_STACK` entry. `destroy()` now marks
    the engine, and `__del__` skips engines that
    were destroyed explicitly. Repeated explicit `destroy()` calls still run
    in full, as `test_destroy_unpin.py`
       requires.
    7. **`lp._hp_grad`** (`bf16_optimizer.py`): `BF16_Optimizer` points
    every parameter at a view of its flat fp32
    gradient buffer, so a kept model pins the whole buffer (2x the bf16
    model size). `destroy()` now clears it.
    
    ## Test
    
    `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py::TestDestroyReleasesEngine`,
    `world_size = 1`, 7 cases: ZeRO-1/2/3, each without and
    with CPU offload, plus `BF16_Optimizer` (ZeRO-1, bf16,
    `grad_accum_dtype: fp32`). Each case checks, while the model is
    kept, that the destroyed engine and optimizer are collected and that no
    parameter still holds the `BF16_Optimizer`
    gradient buffer; that collecting a destroyed engine after a new engine
    wraps the model leaves the new engine's fp32
    parameters unchanged; and that the model is collected once the last
    engine is destroyed.
    
    ## Validation
    ```bash
    cd tests && CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest --forked unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py::TestDestroyReleasesEngine
    ```
    Memory per create/destroy cycle (2 ranks, rank 0, `Sequential` of 16
    `Linear(4096, 4096)`, bf16, torch AdamW, 4 cycles;
    growth = (cycle 4 - cycle 1) / 3; "kept" = the caller keeps every model,
    as HF Trainer does):
    
    | Scenario | Before | After |
    |---|---|---|
    | ZeRO-3, model dropped | +2048.6 MiB GPU | 0 |
    | **ZeRO-3 + CPU offload, model dropped (#7204)** | **+4097.2 MiB host
    RSS** | **+0.4 MiB RSS** |
    | ZeRO-3, model kept | +2048.6 MiB GPU | +256.2 MiB (the kept bf16
    partition) |
    | ZeRO-3 + `zero.Init`, model kept | +2048.6 MiB GPU | +256.2 MiB |
    | ZeRO-3 + CPU offload, model kept | +4097.3 MiB RSS | +512.9 MiB RSS
    (the kept pinned partition, rounded up to a power of two by torch's host
    allocator) |
    | ZeRO-2, model kept | +2048.5 MiB GPU | +512.1 MiB (the kept bf16
    model) |
    | ZeRO-2 + CPU offload, model kept | +544.1 MiB GPU, +3616.6 MiB RSS |
    +512.1 MiB GPU, RSS flat |
    | ZeRO-1, model kept | +2048.5 MiB GPU | +512.1 MiB |
    | ZeRO-0 (`FP16_UnfusedOptimizer`, bf16), model kept | +3584.9 MiB GPU |
    +512.1 MiB |
    | `FP16_Optimizer` (fused Adam, fp16), model kept | +3584.9 MiB GPU |
    +512.1 MiB |
    | `BF16_Optimizer`, model kept | +3072.8 MiB GPU | +512.1 MiB |
    | ZeRO-2, model dropped (control) | 0 | 0 |
    
    After the fix no destroyed engine or optimizer stays alive in any
    scenario. ZeRO-1/2/3 with fp32 gradient accumulation
    also keep only the model. The memory numbers were measured before the
    last commit, which changes only a repeated
    `destroy()`.
    
    ## AI assistance
    
    This change was developed with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot CLI). I
    reviewed every changed line and ran the tests.
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Hongwei Chen <hongweichenmail@gmail.com>

    process group
    - stop at the latest rank-local EOS instead of always decoding to
    `max_new_tokens`

    group. CUDA/HIP graph-capture rollout remains outside this change

    from the default world size, and `_has_unfinished_sequences()` then
    issues an **ungrouped world all-reduce**. A data-parallel subgroup that
    enters rollout while other WORLD ranks stay out would block on that
    collective; concurrently active subgroups would also be coupled
    unnecessarily. The group-aware criterion already gives every rank in the
    parameter-gather group the same stop decision, so the ZeRO-3 path passes
    `synced_gpus=False` and the non-ZeRO-3/FSDP paths keep the Transformers
    default.

Author: Hongwei Chen <33092912+hwchen2017@users.noreply.github.com>

    ## Problem
    `engine.destroy()` does not release the engine: after `destroy()`, `del`

    ## Summary
    
    - synchronize EOS stopping decisions across the ZeRO-3 parameter-gather
    process group
    - stop at the latest rank-local EOS instead of always decoding to
    `max_new_tokens`
    - retain each sequence's first EOS and pad later response positions
    - keep non-ZeRO-3 generation on the native EOS path
    - disable the `synced_gpus` default that Transformers derives from the
    default world size on the ZeRO-3 path
    
    The rendezvous uses `optimizer.dp_process_group`, which is the group
    used by ZeRO-3 parameter gathers, rather than assuming the default world
    group. CUDA/HIP graph-capture rollout remains outside this change
    because it bypasses Hugging Face `generate()`.
    
    ## Why `synced_gpus` must be disabled
    
    When Transformers can observe ZeRO-3 it defaults `synced_gpus` to True
    from the default world size, and `_has_unfinished_sequences()` then
    issues an **ungrouped world all-reduce**. A data-parallel subgroup that
    enters rollout while other WORLD ranks stay out would block on that
    collective; concurrently active subgroups would also be coupled
    unnecessarily. The group-aware criterion already gives every rank in the
    parameter-gather group the same stop decision, so the ZeRO-3 path passes
    `synced_gpus=False` and the non-ZeRO-3/FSDP paths keep the Transformers
    default.

    Size HybridEngine rollout KV caches from local prefill shapes under AutoTP (#9008)
    
    ## Summary
    
    Size HybridEngine rollout KV caches from each rank's own prefill KV
    tensors, not from the global model config. Under AutoTP, each rank holds
    only its share of the KV heads. Today the cache is allocated for the
    full model's KV-head count, so TP>1 rollout fails on all three decode
    paths:
    
    | Path | TP>1 failure today | Change |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Plain graph (`_generate_graph`) | Passing batch size, device and dtype
    makes `DeepSpeedStaticCache` initialize from `module.config` up front,
    so the lazy per-layer setup never runs. The prefill copy then fails with
    `4 vs 2` heads, or broadcasts silently when the rank has 1 local head. |
    Drop those up-front arguments, so the existing lazy setup sizes each
    layer from the prefill tensors before capture. |
    | Continuous eager (`_generate_continuous`) | The same up-front setup
    from config fails on the first prefill copy (`4 vs 2`, `2 vs 8`). |
    Create the cache lazily. `_continuous_cache_layer` initializes each

commit cbed412dc58d4e91435f47868960ab7131042733
Author: Venus-Tzz <1601677496@qq.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 10 09:27:55 2026 +0000

    Use C++20 for CUDA/ROCm op builders on torch 2.12+ (#9041)
    
    ## Summary
    
    On PyTorch 2.12+, `torch.utils.cpp_extension` builds extensions with
    `-std=c++20`, and PyTorch's headers require it. `CUDAOpBuilder.cxx_args`
    already follows that rule (#8238), but `nvcc_args` still chooses the
    device-compiler standard from the installed CUDA toolkit version: CUDA
    12.5+ and CUDA 13+ get C++20, while CUDA 12.0–12.4 get `-std=c++17`.
    That later flag wins, so any JIT build whose `.cu` sources include torch
    headers fails on CUDA 12.0–12.4. For example, `FPQuantizerBuilder` with
    nvcc 12.4 and torch 2.14.1 fails with:
    
    ```
    torch/include/c10/util/intrusive_ptr.h(775): error: namespace "std" has no member "strong_ordering"
    ...
    100 errors detected in the compilation of "csrc/fp_quantizer/fp_quantize_impl.cu".
    ```
    
    This PR makes `CUDAOpBuilder.nvcc_args` use C++20 from CUDA 12.0 when
    torch >= 2.12, keeps the existing toolkit-version rule for older torch,
    and applies the same torch-version rule to the ROCm branch of
    `nvcc_args`.
    
    Scope: the CUDA and ROCm paths of `CUDAOpBuilder.nvcc_args`. The NPU and
    XPU builders already have their own fixes (#8803, #8816); SUPA builders
    do not go through `nvcc_args`. This is the nvcc counterpart of #8238.
    #8422 only covered CUDA 13+, and #5806 left CUDA 12.4 as a TODO ("Fix
    may need to be extended to CUDA 12.4, needs testing").
    
    Duplicate-work check: I did not find an existing issue or PR that
    changes the CUDA 12.0–12.4 nvcc path or the ROCm branch. #8235 tracks
    the broader hardcoded-C++17 problem, #8238 fixed `cxx_args` only, and
    #8422 extended `nvcc_args` to CUDA 13+.
    
    ## Testing
    
    Hardware and versions: 4× NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (two GPUs used), Python
    3.10.22, torch 2.14.1+cu126, nvcc 12.4.131, Triton 3.8.0. Each build
    used a fresh `TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR`.
    
    Before: `FPQuantizerBuilder().load()` fails. nvcc receives `-std=c++17`,
    the build stops on torch's C++20 headers, and no `fp_quantizer.so` is
    produced.
    
    After: the same command succeeds, and the generated `build.ninja` has
    `-std=c++20` in `cuda_cflags`. `QuantizerBuilder` and
    `InferenceBuilder`, which also use the base `nvcc_args`, build
    successfully as well.
    
    Commands:
    
    ```bash
    TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR=<fresh-dir> python -c "from deepspeed.ops.op_builder import FPQuantizerBuilder, QuantizerBuilder, InferenceBuilder; FPQuantizerBuilder().load(); QuantizerBuilder().load(); InferenceBuilder().load()"
    python -m pytest tests/unit/ops/test_op_builder.py -q
    TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR=<fresh-dir> python -m pytest tests/unit/ops/fp_quantizer/test_fp8_gemm.py -q
    ```
    
    Results:
    
    - `tests/unit/ops/test_op_builder.py`: 25 passed, 1 skipped. The 7 new
    parametrized cases cover CUDA 12.0/12.4/12.5, torch 2.11/2.12/2.14, and
    the ROCm branch.
    -
    `tests/unit/ops/fp_quantizer/test_fp8_gemm.py::test_fp8_gemm_decodes_zero_and_subnormal_weights`:
    4 passed.
    - Full `tests/unit/ops/fp_quantizer/test_fp8_gemm.py`: 25 passed, 1
    failed (`test_fp_quant[256-qbits8-bf16]`, error ≈0.009 vs the 0.004
    threshold). The same case fails on `origin/master` (`8b7422e2`) when the
    extension is built with C++20, so it is pre-existing and unrelated to
    this change.
    
    Compatibility: CUDA 12.4 was executed. CUDA 12.0–12.3 and 12.5+ select
    C++20 by the same code path; CUDA ≤ 11 and torch < 2.12 keep their
    previous flags and are covered by the unit tests. ROCm was not executed
    (no ROCm machine available); its branch was changed by the same
    torch-version rule and is covered by unit tests only.
    
    AI assistance was used to prepare this change. The submitter reviewed
    every changed line and ran the tests above.
    
    Signed-off-by: Zizhao Tang <1601677496@qq.com>

    [NPU] Fix the fused LAMB step and inference int4/int8 dequantization on Ascend (#9043)
    
    ## Summary
    
    This fixes two runtime defects in the Ascend NPU op builders added by
    #8627:
    
    1. **Every fp16 LAMB step fails** with `RuntimeError: a leaf Variable
    that requires grad is being used in an in-place operation.` The fused
    LAMB implementation copies the updated fp32 master weight into the fp16
    model parameter with `p_copy.copy_(p.data)`; `p_copy` is a leaf
    parameter that requires grad.
    2. **Every fp16 inference weight dequantization fails** with
    `NotImplementedError: experimental fp_quantizer path is not needed for
    hpZ`. `DeQuantizer.dequantize` takes its fp16 fast path for
    last-dimension groups, but the Ascend quantizer builder never
    implemented the two entry points it calls.
    
    Both failures are currently reported by CI: the affected cases belong to
    the existing unit-test shards, and this PR restores them by fixing the
    NPU implementations, not by skipping or disabling tests.
    
    **Design constraint:** all changes are confined to `op_builder/npu/`. No
    common runtime or inference code is modified.
    
    ## Problem
    
    ### 1. Fused LAMB: in-place copy of a leaf parameter
    
    Call chain:
    
    ```
    tests/unit/... (DistributedTest, world_size=2)
      -> deepspeed/runtime/fp16/unfused_optimizer.py:169  step_fused_lamb
           self.optimizer.step(grads=..., output_params=self.fp16_groups, ...)
      -> deepspeed/ops/lamb/fused_lamb.py:165             FusedLamb.step
           self.fused_lamb_cuda.lamb(p.data, out_p, ...)
      -> op_builder/npu/fused_lamb.py:75                  NPUFusedLamb.lamb
           p_copy.copy_(p.data)                          # <-- raises
    ```
    
    `p_copy` is `out_p`, an fp16 parameter taken from `self.fp16_groups`. It
    is a leaf tensor with `requires_grad=True`, so PyTorch rejects the
    in-place copy. The copy only mirrors the fp32 update into the fp16
    parameter; it is bookkeeping, not part of the autograd graph.
    
    Impact: **6 existing tests** covering FP16 + LAMB, empty gradients, MoE
    gradient norms, dynamic loss scale, and the unfused-optimizer checkpoint
    round-trip fail on Ascend. Any fp16 LAMB training run fails on its first
    step.
    
    ### 2. Inference int4/int8 dequantization: unimplemented entry points
    
    `DeQuantizer.dequantize`
    (`deepspeed/inference/quantization/utils.py:110`) enters the fused fast
    path when all of the following hold:
    
    - `group_size % 8 == 0`
    - `num_bits` is 4 or 8
    - the quantization group is the last dimension
    - the parameter dtype is `torch.float16`
    - the runtime device matches the accelerator device
    
    All of them hold for fp16 inference weights on Ascend, so the dispatcher
    calls `get_quantizer_module().dequantize_int4_to_half_experimental(...)`
    or `dequantize_int8_to_half_experimental(...)`. Both Ascend entry points
    were stubs:
    
    ```python
    raise NotImplementedError("experimental fp_quantizer path is not needed for hpZ")
    ```
    
    The fp32 cases in the same suite pass because `dtype == torch.float16`
    is false; they fall through to the generic `_decompress_uint4_to_uint8`
    + `_dequantize_int8` path. That is the numerical reference this fix
    matches.
    
    Impact: **12 existing tests** fail at this point in CI: the fp16
    int4/int8 round-trips, the `group_dim=1` `QuantizedLinear` cases, and
    the ZeRO-3 post-init / quantized-initialization cases (including CPU
    offload). Inference weight quantization cannot be used on Ascend.
    
    ### Scope note: the shared int4 packer requires CANN 9.0.0
    
    The shared `Quantizer._compress_uint8_to_uint4` uses a uint8 left shift,
    which CANN provides as `aclnnLeftShifts` from 9.0.0. The validation host
    originally used a manual CANN 8.5.1 installation and int4 failed there
    before dequantization; the conda toolkit was then reinstalled to **CANN
    9.0.1** (`ascend-cann-toolkit` + `ascend-cann-910b-ops` 9.0.1), and the
    int4 cases now run end to end. CI uses CANN 9.0.0 (`cann:latest`), so it
    satisfies the same requirement.
    
    Fixing this on older CANN would require changing
    `deepspeed/inference/quantization/utils.py`, which is common inference
    code. This PR deliberately leaves it untouched; the requirement is
    documented instead (see the next section).
    
    ### CANN version note
    
    `aclnnLeftShifts` is provided by CANN 9.0.0 and later. Both environments
    satisfy this: local validation runs CANN 9.0.1, and CI uses the floating
    `swr.cn-southwest-2.myhuaweicloud.com/base_image/ascend-ci/cann:latest`
    image, whose 2026-11-09 `ds_report` output reports `ascend_cann version
    9.0.0`. The image tag is not pinned and the workflows do not assert the
    version, but the current image has the operator.
    
    The version can be queried through torch_npu:
    
    ```python
    from torch_npu.utils import get_cann_version
    get_cann_version()                                     # '9.0.1' locally, '9.0.0' in CI
    
    from torch_npu.npu.utils import _is_gte_cann_version
    _is_gte_cann_version('9.0.0', module='CANN')           # True locally and in CI
    ```
    
    No runtime gate is added: `torch.bitwise_left_shift` is the interface
    and dispatches to `aclnnLeftShifts` directly, which is exactly the call
    the shared packer already makes. The NPU dequantizers below are
    version-independent and are called directly by the existing fast path.
    
    The operator's support matrix covers this workload: the ACLNN
    documentation lists
    `INT8`/`INT16`/`INT32`/`INT64`/`UINT8`/`UINT16`/`UINT32`/`UINT64`
    inputs, a scalar `shiftBits`, non-contiguous tensors, and support on
    Atlas A2/A3/350 products. The 910B4 is an Atlas A2 device; the packer's
    input is `uint8` in `[0, 15]` and the shift amount is the scalar `4`,
    within the documented precision guarantee (`shiftBits` below the dtype
    width).
    
    torch_npu's own int4 packing APIs use a different wire format from
    DeepSpeed's inference format, so they are not drop-in substitutes:
    
    | torch_npu API | Layout |
    |---|---|
    | `torch_npu.npu_convert_weight_to_int4pack` | signed `[-8, 7]`, low
    nibble first, 8 values per `int32` |
    | `torch_npu.npu_quantize(..., dtype=torch.quint4x2)` | low nibble
    first, clamped to the signed int4 range, `int32` output |
    | `torch_npu.npu_anti_quant` | consumes int32-packed int4 (8 values per
    int32), same low-nibble-first layout |
    
    DeepSpeed inference stores unsigned `[0, 15]` values, high nibble first,
    two per `uint8`. Reusing the torch_npu APIs would require nibble
    swapping and a `-8` offset, and the result would still have to be called
    from the shared packer, so this PR leaves them unused.
    
    ## Fix
    
    ### Fused LAMB (`op_builder/npu/fused_lamb.py`)
    
    ```python
    p.data.copy_((p.float() - step_size * lamb_coeff * update).to(p.dtype))
    if p_copy.numel() > 0:
        # p_copy is a leaf fp16 parameter and the copy only mirrors the
        # fp32 update into it, so it must not be recorded by autograd.
        with torch.no_grad():
            p_copy.copy_(p.data)
    ```
    
    Only the copy is wrapped; the rest of the update stays outside
    `no_grad`. The other in-place operations in `lamb()` (on `exp_avg`,
    `exp_avg_sq`, and `p.data`) were checked: the state tensors do not
    require grad, and `p.data.copy_` already bypasses autograd.
    
    ### Inference dequantizers (`op_builder/npu/quantizer.py`)
    
    Both entry points now implement the asymmetric inference formula `value
    / scale + min` in pure torch:
    
    ```python
    @staticmethod
    def _dequantize_inference_groups(values, scale_buffer, min_val_buffer, num_group, group_size):
        scale = scale_buffer.reshape(num_group, 1).to(torch.float16)
        min_val = min_val_buffer.reshape(num_group, 1).to(torch.float16)
        values = values.reshape(num_group, group_size).to(torch.float16)
        return values.div_(scale).add_(min_val)
    ```
    
    The int4 entry point unpacks two unsigned nibbles per byte, **high
    nibble first** (even element in the high nibble, odd element in the low
    nibble), matching `Quantizer._compress_uint8_to_uint4`. It stays in
    `uint8` while unpacking and only then converts to fp16, so the temporary
    is one byte per element rather than the eight bytes an `int64` unpack
    would use.
    
    This is deliberately **not** reusing `NPUQuantizer._unpack_int4`: that
    helper belongs to the Zero++/hpZ wire format, which packs the even
    element in the low nibble and sign-extends each nibble. The inference
    format is high-nibble-first and unsigned (`0..15`); using the hpZ
    unpacker would swap elements and turn values above 7 into negatives.
    
    The implementation keeps the shared dispatcher unchanged and requires no
    new capability flag: the two entry points are exactly the contract the
    existing fast path calls. Their output is bitwise identical to the
    generic reference path (verified below), so no numerical branch is
    introduced.
    
    ### CANN version guard (`op_builder/npu/quantizer.py`)
    
    The int4 dequantizer calls
    `NPUQuantizer._check_int4_inference_support()` before unpacking. The
    check uses `torch_npu.npu.utils._is_gte_cann_version("9.0.0",
    module="CANN")` when available and falls back to parsing
    `torch_npu.utils.get_cann_version()`; it caches the result per process
    and fails open when the version cannot be determined. On CANN older than
    9.0.0 (including 8.5.x) it raises a `RuntimeError` with the detected
    version and upgrade advice; on 9.0.0+ it returns and the normal path
    continues.
    
    Boundary: in the standard inference flow the shared packer runs before
    this entry point, so on CANN 8.5 the first error can still be the
    missing `aclnnLeftShifts`. The guard covers pre-packed weights and
    direct calls to the NPU entry point, and makes the version requirement
    explicit. Intercepting the shared packer itself would require a
    common-code hook, which this NPU-only change intentionally avoids.

    Use C++20 for CUDA/ROCm op builders on torch 2.12+ (#9041)
    
    ## Summary
    
    On PyTorch 2.12+, `torch.utils.cpp_extension` builds extensions with
    `-std=c++20`, and PyTorch's headers require it. `CUDAOpBuilder.cxx_args`
    already follows that rule (#8238), but `nvcc_args` still chooses the
    device-compiler standard from the installed CUDA toolkit version: CUDA
    12.5+ and CUDA 13+ get C++20, while CUDA 12.0–12.4 get `-std=c++17`.
    That later flag wins, so any JIT build whose `.cu` sources include torch
    headers fails on CUDA 12.0–12.4. For example, `FPQuantizerBuilder` with
    nvcc 12.4 and torch 2.14.1 fails with:
    
    ```
    torch/include/c10/util/intrusive_ptr.h(775): error: namespace "std" has no member "strong_ordering"
    ...
    100 errors detected in the compilation of "csrc/fp_quantizer/fp_quantize_impl.cu".
    ```
    
    This PR makes `CUDAOpBuilder.nvcc_args` use C++20 from CUDA 12.0 when
    torch >= 2.12, keeps the existing toolkit-version rule for older torch,
    and applies the same torch-version rule to the ROCm branch of
    `nvcc_args`.
    
    Scope: the CUDA and ROCm paths of `CUDAOpBuilder.nvcc_args`. The NPU and
    XPU builders already have their own fixes (#8803, #8816); SUPA builders
    do not go through `nvcc_args`. This is the nvcc counterpart of #8238.
    #8422 only covered CUDA 13+, and #5806 left CUDA 12.4 as a TODO ("Fix
    may need to be extended to CUDA 12.4, needs testing").
    
    Duplicate-work check: I did not find an existing issue or PR that
    changes the CUDA 12.0–12.4 nvcc path or the ROCm branch. #8235 tracks
    the broader hardcoded-C++17 problem, #8238 fixed `cxx_args` only, and
    #8422 extended `nvcc_args` to CUDA 13+.

    Use C++20 for CUDA/ROCm op builders on torch 2.12+ (#9041)
    
    ## Summary
    
    On PyTorch 2.12+, `torch.utils.cpp_extension` builds extensions with
    `-std=c++20`, and PyTorch's headers require it. `CUDAOpBuilder.cxx_args`
    already follows that rule (#8238), but `nvcc_args` still chooses the
    device-compiler standard from the installed CUDA toolkit version: CUDA
    12.5+ and CUDA 13+ get C++20, while CUDA 12.0–12.4 get `-std=c++17`.
    That later flag wins, so any JIT build whose `.cu` sources include torch
    headers fails on CUDA 12.0–12.4. For example, `FPQuantizerBuilder` with
    nvcc 12.4 and torch 2.14.1 fails with:
    
    ```
    torch/include/c10/util/intrusive_ptr.h(775): error: namespace "std" has no member "strong_ordering"
    ...
    100 errors detected in the compilation of "csrc/fp_quantizer/fp_quantize_impl.cu".
    ```
    
    This PR makes `CUDAOpBuilder.nvcc_args` use C++20 from CUDA 12.0 when
    torch >= 2.12, keeps the existing toolkit-version rule for older torch,
    and applies the same torch-version rule to the ROCm branch of
    `nvcc_args`.
    
    Scope: the CUDA and ROCm paths of `CUDAOpBuilder.nvcc_args`. The NPU and
    XPU builders already have their own fixes (#8803, #8816); SUPA builders
    do not go through `nvcc_args`. This is the nvcc counterpart of #8238.
    #8422 only covered CUDA 13+, and #5806 left CUDA 12.4 as a TODO ("Fix
    may need to be extended to CUDA 12.4, needs testing").
    
    Duplicate-work check: I did not find an existing issue or PR that
    changes the CUDA 12.0–12.4 nvcc path or the ROCm branch. #8235 tracks
    the broader hardcoded-C++17 problem, #8238 fixed `cxx_args` only, and
    #8422 extended `nvcc_args` to CUDA 13+.

    3.10.22, torch 2.14.1+cu126, nvcc 12.4.131, Triton 3.8.0. Each build

    produced.

    `-std=c++20` in `cuda_cflags`. `QuantizerBuilder` and
